headline_marked: Anthropic finds [[Claude AI has internal 'thought' space]] like human brain
headline: Anthropic finds Claude AI has internal 'thought' space like human brain
summary: Anthropic's research reveals Claude AI's internal 'J-Space' works like human consciousness
details: Anthropic has discovered that its Claude AI models use an internal reasoning space, called 'J-Space', which mirrors some of the internal processing of human consciousness. This space allows Claude to analyze and manipulate concepts and ideas before broadcasting them to impact the eventual prompt outputs.

The J-Space acts like a 'global workspace' that can collect together multi-sensory inputs unconsciously, and thrust them into the fore when relevant. This workspace is accessible to a wide range of networks within the model, allowing the information it surfaces to be disseminated throughout the most relevant processes.

Anthropic used its Jacobian Lens technique to map internal activations onto words in the model's output vocabulary, making the J-Space readable. This technique allowed researchers to observe each step of a multi-step math calculation being handled individually, producing multiple results which led to the final answer.
caption:
Can AI models really think like humans? New research says yes

Anthropic has discovered that its Claude AI models use an internal reasoning space, called 'J-Space', which mirrors some of the internal processing of human consciousness. This space allows Claude to analyze and manipulate concepts and ideas before broadcasting them to impact the eventual prompt outputs.

The J-Space acts like a 'global workspace' that can collect together multi-sensory inputs unconsciously, and thrust them into the fore when relevant. This workspace is accessible to a wide range of networks within the model, allowing the information it surfaces to be disseminated throughout the most relevant processes.

Anthropic used its Jacobian Lens technique to map internal activations onto words in the model's output vocabulary, making the J-Space readable. This technique allowed researchers to observe each step of a multi-step math calculation being handled individually, producing multiple results which led to the final answer.

headline: Snails' Teeth Stronger than Spider Silk Found
summary: Marine snails' teeth are the strongest natural material on Earth.
details: Marine snails, commonly called limpets, have teeth made of a mixture of goethite nanofibers encased in a protein matrix. These teeth are about five times stronger than most spider silk.
The tooth material can withstand pressure that would turn carbon into diamond, comparable to a single strand of spaghetti holding up about 3,300 one-pound bags of sugar.
The researchers published their findings in the Journal of the Royal Society Interface, and this discovery could inspire the development of new materials.
caption:
What if the strongest natural material wasn't what you expected? Snails' teeth are now known to be the strongest natural material on Earth.

Marine snails, commonly called limpets, have teeth made of a mixture of goethite nanofibers encased in a protein matrix. These teeth are about five times stronger than most spider silk.

The tooth material can withstand pressure that would turn carbon into diamond, comparable to a single strand of spaghetti holding up about 3,300 one-pound bags of sugar.

The researchers published their findings in the Journal of the Royal Society Interface, and this discovery could inspire the development of new materials.
